office: West Valley-Mission Community College District Board of Trustees, Area 7
summary: The West Valley-Mission Community College District runs West Valley College in Saratoga and Mission College in Santa Clara. Its elected board of trustees sets the budget, hires the chancellor, and oversees bond-funded construction. Each trustee is elected by one trustee area. This is a single-seat, nonpartisan, one-round election: whoever gets more votes on November 3 wins, with no primary. Incumbent Susan Oster Fish, an attorney and registered nurse first elected in 2016, faces Doug Robb, a San Jose City College kinesiology instructor and baseball coach.

positions.stance: Board vice president; chairs the district's Audit and Budget Oversight Committee and sits on the Mission-West Valley Land Corporation Investment Committee. (District trustee page)
Credited with helping bring the College of Adaptive Arts, which serves adults with disabilities, to the West Valley campus. (District trustee page)
This research did not find a published 2026 campaign platform from Fish beyond her district biography.

Wants smaller classes, more sections, and schedules that work for part-time, working, and evening students. His union backers say 10% to 20% of students are waitlisted each semester and that new sections should open quickly when waitlists form. (Campaign website; AFT 6157)

Wants hiring shifted from administrators to faculty and student-facing staff, retirements backfilled, and money focused on instruction rather than construction. AFT 6157 says the district's unrestricted ending fund balance grew from about $10.8 million (2013) to $122.7 million (2026) and cites a State Auditor finding that administrators more than doubled while faculty fell 7%. These are the union's figures and were not independently checked here. (Campaign website; AFT 6157)
Wants faculty and staff to have a bigger voice in institutional decisions. (Campaign website)

key_differences: Insider versus faculty challenger: Fish has been a trustee since 2016 and chairs the district's audit committee; Robb is a longtime community-college instructor running on reallocating money from administration and reserves to classes.

Reserves and spending: Robb's campaign and union argue the district is sitting on too large a reserve and over-investing in administration and construction. This research found no published response from Fish.

Robb teaches at San Jose City College, in the neighboring San José-Evergreen district, and his main institutional backer is that college's faculty union (AFT 6157). Fish is a West Valley College graduate and the parent of two West Valley graduates.
